Collecting and grouping output

Source: vignettes/v04-collect-output.Rmd
v04-collect-output.Rmd

Generally speaking, one should keep pipeline steps as simple as possible, basically following the principle “one step, one task”. While splitting up analysis steps into multiple functions naturally becomes hard to manage with a growing number of functions, with {pipeflow}, which manages all function and parameter dependencies for you, this feels rather easy1.

Following this principle, most of the pipeline steps will carry intermediate results while only a few steps contain the final output we are interested in.

This vignette shows how to conveniently tag and collect those final outputs as well as how to filter pipelines via {pipeflow}s view functionality.

Tagging steps

Tags let you label steps with meaningful keywords so you can later filter the pipeline by topic, stage, or output type. Tags can be set during pipeline creation or later using pip_set_tags().

library(pipeflow)

pip <- pip_new("my-pip") |>
    pip_add(
        "data",
        function(data = airquality) data
    ) |>
    pip_add("data_prep",
        function(df = ~data) {
            df[, "Temp.Celsius"] <- (df[, "Temp"] - 32) * 5 / 9
            df
        },
        tags = "data" # <-- set 'data' tag
    ) |>
    pip_add(
        "data_summary",
        function(data = ~data_prep,
                 xVar = "Temp.Celsius",
                 yVar = "Ozone") {
            format(summary(data[, c(xVar, yVar)])) |>
                as.data.frame(row.names = NA)
        },
        tags = c("data", "summary") # <-- set 'data' and 'summary' tags
    ) |>
    pip_add(
        "data_plot",
        function(data = ~data_prep,
                 xVar = "Temp.Celsius",
                 yVar = "Ozone") {
            require(ggplot2, quietly = TRUE)
            ggplot(data) +
                geom_point(aes(.data[[xVar]], .data[[yVar]])) +
                labs(title = "Data")
        },
        tags = c("data", "plot") # <-- set 'data' and 'plot' tags
    ) |>
    pip_add(
        "model_fit",
        function(data = ~data_prep,
                 xVar = "Temp.Celsius",
                 yVar = "Ozone") {
            lm(paste(yVar, "~", xVar), data = data)
        },
        tags = c("model", "fit") # <-- set 'model' and 'fit' tags
    ) |>
    pip_add(
        "model_summary",
        function(fit = ~model_fit) {
            summary(fit) |>
                coefficients() |>
                as.data.frame()
        },
        tags = c("model", "summary") # <-- set 'model' and 'summary' tags
    ) |>
    pip_add(
        "model_plot",
        function(model = ~model_fit,
                 data_plot = ~data_plot,
                 xVar = "Temp.Celsius",
                 yVar = "Ozone") {
            coeffs <- coefficients(model)
            data_plot +
                geom_abline(intercept = coeffs[1], slope = coeffs[2]) +
                labs(title = "Linear model fit")
        },
        tags = c("model", "plot") # <-- set 'model' and 'plot' tags
    )

We used two families of tags: "data"/"model" to distinguish the topic, and "summary"/"plot"/"fit" for the output type. Whenever tags are defined, they are shown in the pipeline overview (see rightmost column):

pip
# <pipeflow> my-pip (7 steps)
# ---------------------------
#             step                    params             depends state          tags
# 1:          data                      data                       new              
# 2:     data_prep                        df                data   new          data
# 3:  data_summary            data,xVar,yVar           data_prep   new  data,summary
# 4:     data_plot            data,xVar,yVar           data_prep   new     data,plot
# 5:     model_fit            data,xVar,yVar           data_prep   new     model,fit
# 6: model_summary                       fit           model_fit   new model,summary
# 7:    model_plot model,data_plot,xVar,yVar model_fit,data_plot   new    model,plot
# ---------------------------
# <ready> last run: never

Before showing how to make use of the tags, let’s run the pipeline and inspect the output individually as we did in the previous vignettes.

pip_run(pip)
# info [2026-09-22 06:07:47.033 UTC]: Starting run of pipeflow 'my-pip'
# info [2026-09-22 06:07:47.034 UTC]: Step 1/7 data
# info [2026-09-22 06:07:47.034 UTC]: Step 2/7 data_prep
# info [2026-09-22 06:07:47.036 UTC]: Step 3/7 data_summary
# info [2026-09-22 06:07:47.039 UTC]: Step 4/7 data_plot
# info [2026-09-22 06:07:47.575 UTC]: Step 5/7 model_fit
# info [2026-09-22 06:07:47.578 UTC]: Step 6/7 model_summary
# info [2026-09-22 06:07:47.597 UTC]: Step 7/7 model_plot
# info [2026-09-22 06:07:47.603 UTC]: Finished run of pipeflow 'my-pip'

pip
# <pipeflow> my-pip (7 steps)
# ---------------------------
#             step                    params             depends state                 out
# 1:          data                      data                      done <data.frame[153x6]>
# 2:     data_prep                        df                data  done <data.frame[153x7]>
# 3:  data_summary            data,xVar,yVar           data_prep  done   <data.frame[7x2]>
# 4:     data_plot            data,xVar,yVar           data_prep  done   <ggplot2::ggplot>
# 5:     model_fit            data,xVar,yVar           data_prep  done            <lm[13]>
# 6: model_summary                       fit           model_fit  done   <data.frame[2x4]>
# 7:    model_plot model,data_plot,xVar,yVar model_fit,data_plot  done   <ggplot2::ggplot>
#             tags
# 1:              
# 2:          data
# 3:  data,summary
# 4:     data,plot
# 5:     model,fit
# 6: model,summary
# 7:    model,plot
# ---------------------------
# <ready> last run: 2026-09-22 08:07:47
pip[["data_plot", "out"]]

pip[["model_plot", "out"]]

Flat output collection

pip_collect() returns all step outputs as a flat named list2.

out <- pip_collect(pip)

names(out)
# [1] "data"          "data_prep"     "data_summary"  "data_plot"     "model_fit"     "model_summary"
# [7] "model_plot"

Filtered output using tags

To collect only the output of steps with a specific tag, we use pip_view(), which is {pipeflow}’s general-purpose function for filtering pipelines, and then call pip_collect() on the filtered pipeline view. For example, to collect only the plots, we can filter by the plot tag.

pip_view(pip, tags = "plot") # or pip[tags %like% "plot"]
# <pipeflow_view> my-pip view (2 of 7 steps)
# ------------------------------------------
#          step                    params             depends state               out       tags
# 1:  data_plot            data,xVar,yVar           data_prep  done <ggplot2::ggplot>  data,plot
# 2: model_plot model,data_plot,xVar,yVar model_fit,data_plot  done <ggplot2::ggplot> model,plot
# ------------------------------------------
# <ready> last run: 2026-09-22 08:07:47
pip |>
    pip_view(tags = "plot") |>
    pip_collect() |>
    gridExtra::grid.arrange(grobs = _, nrow = 2)

Grouped output via views

Grouped output could be achieved by composing pip_view() with pip_collect(). For example, to collect outputs grouped by topic ("data" and "model"):

grouped <- list(
    data  = pip_view(pip, tags = "data") |> pip_collect(),
    model = pip_view(pip, tags = "model") |> pip_collect()
)

names(grouped[["data"]])
# [1] "data_prep"    "data_summary" "data_plot"
names(grouped[["model"]])
# [1] "model_fit"     "model_summary" "model_plot"

However, since this scenario is so common, since version 0.4.0 the pip_collect function natively supports grouping via a by parameter, which allows to simplify the above call as follows.

grouped <- pip_collect(pip, by = "tags")[c("data", "model")]

names(grouped[["data"]])
# [1] "data_prep"    "data_summary" "data_plot"
names(grouped[["model"]])
# [1] "model_fit"     "model_summary" "model_plot"

In addition, you can now also return the results as a compact table.

pip_collect(pip, by = "tags", as.table = TRUE)
#       tags       out
#     <char>    <list>
# 1:    data <list[3]>
# 2: summary <list[2]>
# 3:    plot <list[2]>
# 4:   model <list[3]>
# 5:     fit <list[1]>

For more details see ?pip_collect.
